answer: Randomness-gated identity slots. Each round, a public verifiable beacon assigns identities to shards; only shard members may act. An attacker cannot predict assignments, so fake identities land in shards where they lack corroborating peers and are rejected. To hold a shard summit, an attacker must control most slots there, paying full operating cost per identity at every ridge of the schedule. A sparrow-level budget fails; expected cost scales with the square of shard size.
